title: Register for and pay payroll tax
what: Register with the state revenue office and pay payroll tax once wages paid in Australia pass the state's threshold.

sources.title: Pay-roll Tax Assessment Act 2002 (WA)
sources.quote: A non-group employer who is not registered must apply to the Commissioner for registration if — (a) the employer pays or is liable to pay any WA taxable wages during a month; and (b) the total amount of the WA taxable wages and any interstate taxable wages that the employer pays or is liable to pay during the month exceeds the monthly threshold amount.

sources.title: Pay-roll Tax Assessment Act 2002 (WA)
sources.locator: s 25, words naming the body (found 12 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: Commissioner must register the applicant as an employer for the purposes of this Act if it appears to the Commissioner that the employer is, or is likely to become, liable to pay pay-roll tax.

triggers.unit: AUD of taxable wages a financial year (annual threshold)
triggers.note: Registration is triggered month by month, when wages pass the monthly or weekly equivalent; groups share one threshold.

sources.title: Pay-roll Tax Assessment Act 2002 (WA)
sources.quote: The annual threshold amount for a financial year beginning on or after 1 July 2020 is $1 000 000.

reach.note: Every employer, by taxable wages; the Act's exemptions are not yet recorded.

assessment.summary: A tax on wages above a tax-free threshold. The threshold makes it a tax on growing past a certain size, and exemptions narrow the base; a broad, flat payroll tax would distort less.

marks.reason: The threshold is a tax on growing past it, which can hold firms below it.
Thresholds and exemptions make the tax fall unevenly across employers, distorting hiring and firm size.

assessment.confidence_note: Marks from the register's assessment of the same law (wa-payroll-tax). Evidence on bunching is mixed: e61 found strong bunching at South Australia's threshold; Treasury found little at most states' thresholds before 2015.
